response.rationale: The dynamic T-wave changes (deeply inverted then upright) in V2-V4 with normal troponin and exertional chest pain relieved by rest strongly support unstable angina (Wellens' syndrome) due to critical LAD occlusion. NSTEMI is less likely given normal troponin and lack of ST elevation; stable angina is contradicted by the dynamic ECG changes; vasospastic angina is contradicted by exertional pattern and non-ST-elevation ECG; myocarditis is unlikely due to normal troponin and typical ischemic ECG pattern.
